whatChanged: NEW: Monomoy Capital makes an unsolicited $101-a-share cash proposal for LCI Industries; LCI's board rejects it as not superior and backs its Patrick Industries merger (lcii-monomoy-takeover-proposal)
ADVANCED: Marvell signs a $115bn all-stock deal to buy Lumentum at 4.5 Marvell shares each, ~24% premium (mrvl-lumentum-acquisition) (rumored → confirmed)
ADVANCED: Kimberly-Clark completes its acquisition of Kenvue; Kenvue delisted from NYSE (kmb-kenvue-acquisition) (approved → closed)

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsors, strategics and insiders keep taking listed businesses off public markets. Thrive Holdings agreed to buy ADT for $10 a share in cash, about $15.3bn including debt, with a go-shop to 28 November (adt-thrive-take-private). A Trian-led group, Wendy's largest shareholder, offered $7.35 a share to take the chain private (wen-trian-take-private). Bon Secours Mercy Health agreed to buy Surgery Partners at $23.50 a share while Bain keeps its stake (sgry-bon-secours-take-private). EQT signed a board-recommended €46.50-a-share cash offer for Qiagen (qgen-eqt-take-private), and EQT Infrastructure signed a A$3.095-a-share scheme for Cleanaway (cwy-eqt-infrastructure-take-private). Penske Corporation and Mitsui are buying out the Penske Automotive float (pag-penske-mitsui-take-private), a GTCR-led consortium with Elliott is buying CCC Intelligent Solutions (cccs-gtcr-elliott-take-private), and Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint is buying Varonis (vrns-proofpoint-acquisition). India's Affle agreed to buy Perion for $11.70 a share in cash and delist it from Nasdaq and TASE (peri-affle-acquisition), and Cencora is buying out American Oncology Network (cor-aon-acquisition). Tata's Iveco offer has cleared its 80% threshold (ivg-tata-motors-takeover-offer). New approaches keep coming: Monomoy offered $101 a share in cash for LCI Industries, which the board rejected in favour of its signed Patrick merger (lcii-monomoy-takeover-proposal); AVID has topped Warburg Pincus for Ingenia (ina-avid-takeover-proposal), and Challenger rejected a A$11.80 bid from its largest shareholder, TAL Daiichi Life (cgf-tal-daiichi-takeover-proposal). EP Group's Fnac Darty tender closes on 9 November with EU clearance in hand (fnac-ep-group-takeover-bid), while Aurora's board continues to resist Curaleaf's hostile bid (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Regulators, politicians and courts, not the parties, keep deciding deals. Kimberly-Clark closed its Kenvue purchase on 2 November, but only after paying for EU and Australian clearance with feminine-care divestments and sitting through China's in-depth SAMR review (kmb-kenvue-acquisition). AkzoNobel and Axalta have formally offered EU remedies, including selling AkzoNobel's European refinish business, with the Commission's provisional deadline on 6 November (akza-axalta-merger). The ECB has cleared UniCredit to control Commerzbank, but Berlin still opposes it (cbk-unicredit-takeover), and it has also authorised Intesa to control Monte dei Paschi; Consob and Italy's antitrust authority, which may demand extra branch sales, are the remaining gatekeepers (isp-bmps-takeover-offer). DoorDash's $17bn Instacart deal is already drawing antitrust warnings, with closing not expected before late 2027 (cart-doordash-uber-acquisition), and Marvell's newly signed $115bn Lumentum deal is not expected to close until the first half of 2028 (mrvl-lumentum-acquisition). EP Group's Fnac Darty bid needed EU merger clearance (fnac-ep-group-takeover-bid).

themes.label: Large-caps scaling up buybacks on surplus cash
themes.note: Companies with surplus capital keep expanding buybacks, each tying the larger programme to a specific capital tailwind. GM authorized a new $20bn buyback with its Q3 results (gm-buyback-2026), and Simpson Manufacturing replaced a $200m authorization with $1.0bn (ssd-buyback-2026).

themes.label: European incumbents consolidating domestic rivals for scale
themes.note: Europe's large banks, industrials and grocers are buying rivals to reach the scale of US and Chinese peers, while controlling shareholders, governments and supervisors decide the outcomes. Evonik's board formally refused on 30 October to negotiate over BASF's €24-a-share approach, about €11.2bn, so RAG-Stiftung's ~44% stake is now the decisive lever (evk-basf-acquisition). The ECB has cleared UniCredit to go past 30% of Commerzbank despite Berlin's opposition (cbk-unicredit-takeover). Intesa Sanpaolo has ECB authorisation for its sweetened, Delfin-backed offer for Monte dei Paschi, and MPS holders on 29 October voted down the CEO's rival bids for Banco BPM and Banca Generali, clearing Intesa's path (isp-bmps-takeover-offer). Ahold Delhaize is buying Tesco's Czech and Slovak arm to make its Albert chain Czechia's market leader (ad-tesco-cz-sk-acquisition).

themes.label: Governments selling state-held stakes to strategic and financial buyers
themes.note: Governments are privatising long-held stakes and picking buyers on both price and industrial plan. India's cabinet approved selling 60.72% of IDBI Bank to Fairfax (ffh-idbi-bank-acquisition), and Portugal chose Lufthansa's all-cash offer for 44.9% of TAP Air Portugal while keeping a 50.1% majority (lha-tap-stake-acquisition).
